page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m16-vws.5xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 20 vCPUs across 10 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes 33 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 92.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.6 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, requiring network-attached storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1105.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 929.0, both placing in the bottom tier. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 14732.17 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6611.0. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with uncached read speeds at 81.06 GB/sec and write speeds at 49.22 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also perform within average ranges, with Redis SET operations reaching 14.5 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.vgn6i-m16-vws.5xlarge offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of high-end accelerator instances. The combination of 20 dedicated vCPUs, 92 GB of RAM, and an NVIDIA T4 GPU makes it suitable for workloads such as entry-level machine learning inference, video transcoding, virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), and moderately parallelized compute tasks. The lack of local storage means users must factor in the performance and cost of external block storage for data-heavy operations.
